newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy names Albania mission "Operation Alba".
newsitem.headline: Italy names Albania mission "Operation Alba".

text.p: The multinational security force Italy plans to lead into Albania will be called "Operation Alba", the Italian for "sunrise", the Defence Ministry said on Monday.
A ministry spokesman said the word echoed the start of the name of the troubled Balkan state. "It could also signify a new dawn," he said.

Italy has said it plans to start deploying the U.N.-approved force from next week to protect shipments of food and medicines needed in Europe's poorest state after lawless violence broke out last month following the collapse of shady savings schemes.

The name of the mission, beginning with "a", also reflects the fact that it will be the first time Rome has led an international force, although it has taken part in past peace missions in Somalia, Mozambique and Bosnia.
Up to 2,500 of the force's planned 6,000 troops are expected to be Italian. France has pledged 1,000, Greece 700, Turkey 500, Romania 400 and Spain 300. Austria and Denmark may also join.
